Amazon.Built-in core (outside the bag): sku only — a URL path parameter, never a schema attribute. The read model projects scalars beside the bag: ItemSummaryByMarketplace.brand · itemName · manufacturer · color · size · style + first-class identifiers, images, dimensions, classifications, relationships, salesRanks.
Amazon.Extension (the attribute): Everything else is a property of the product-type JSON Schema, in seven property groups: offer (price = list_price) · images · shipping (weight, dimensions) · variations · safety_and_compliance · product_identity (item_name, brand, external_product_id, product_type, …) · product_details. Bag declared open: ItemAttributes {additionalProperties: true}.
Amazon.Definition ↔ value: Modelled as Attribute (name PK) + ProductTypeAttribute join {marketplaceId, parentageLevel, requiredness} — requiredness is a property of the join. JSON-side type / constraints / enum ❓UNKNOWN. 2,336 distinct attribute names; 213 types → 208 attributes, 1,154 pairs, 107 used by one type.
Amazon.A value is stored as: an array of objects per attribute — [{value, marketplace_id, language_tag}] — scalar inside; per-marketplace selectors.
Amazon.Brand: an attribute (product_identity) and a read scalar and a search refinement; must match across a family (“non-varying attributes”).

Shopify.Built-in core (outside the bag): Product 83 fields, ProductVariant 52: title, handle, descriptionHtml, productType (free text), vendor, tags, category, options; variant: price, compareAtPrice, sku, barcode, inventoryItem. Weight is not on the variant — inventoryItem.measurement.weight {unit: WeightUnit!, value: Float!}.
Shopify.Extension (the attribute): MetafieldDefinition (17 fields; ownerType ∈ 26 values incl. PRODUCT, PRODUCTVARIANT). Second surface: the taxonomy — 8,240 base + 316 extended attributes, 93,007 category→attribute edges, 74,820 values.
Shopify.Definition ↔ value: separate objects; a value may exist with definition: null (undefined namespace/key accepted, userErrors: []).
Shopify.A value is stored as: always a string — “the value is always entered and stored as a string, regardless of type”; 48 basic + 12 reference + 53 list types decide parsing.
Shopify.Brand: vendor: String!, free text, no validation; “brand” occurs zero times in the record.

Google.Built-in core (outside the bag): there is only the bag: 145 flat properties on products_v1 — title, description, price, gtins, brand, productWeight, productLength/Height/Width, shippingWeight, googleProductCategory, productTypes, color, size, material, pattern, itemGroupId, …
Google.Extension (the attribute): four open name/value bags: customAttributes (≤2,500, 102.4 kB, recursive) · productDetails {sectionName, attributeName, attributeValue} (≤100; suggested keys incl. Flavor, Scent) · variantOptions {name, value} · cloudExportAdditionalProperties.
Google.Definition ↔ value: no definition object — the 145 names are the schema; the bags carry no definition.
Google.A value is stored as: a typed field (some enums) for the 145; a free string for the bags.
Google.Brand: a flat field, max 70 chars, required except movies/books/music.
Google.Cap: 2,500 custom attributes / 102.4 kB; 100 product details; 30 variant options.

eBay.Built-in core (outside the bag): Inventory Product: brand, ean, epid, isbn, mpn, upc (every identifier variant-level), title, description, imageUrls, subtitle, videoIds. Price/quantity on the Offer.
eBay.Extension (the attribute): the aspect, owned by the leaf category — 197,046 over 15,111 leaves; no id: an item's aspects are {name: [strings]}.
eBay.Definition ↔ value: definition = AspectConstraint (exactly 11 properties), identified only by localizedAspectName within a category — a per-category definition without an identity.
eBay.A value is stored as: strings in an array, per aspect name, on each SKU; aspectDataType STRING 196,549 / NUMBER 482 / DATE 15.
eBay.Brand: built-in Product.brand and a Brand aspect; catalog-matched aspects are auto-filled and locked.
eBay.Cap: name 40 chars · value 50 · 30 values per multi-value aspect; aspects per item not published.
eBay.Example:
● 
"localizedAspects": [{"type": "STRING", "name": "Color", "value": "Blue"}, {"type": "STRING", "name": "Size", "value": "S"},
                     {"type": "STRING", "name": "Brand", "value": "Unbranded"}]
(sandbox Browse item, #11045 §2c); write side ◇ "aspects": {"Color": ["Blue"], "Number in Pack": ["6"]}

Walmart.Extension (the attribute): Visible.<ProductType> — the per-type attribute set where merchandising lives (productName, brand, shortDescription, mainImageUrl, netContent, flavor …); 6,967 types · 383,947 slots · 6,576 names · 28–183 per type.
Walmart.Definition ↔ value: no definition object on the write path — every attribute written out in full per type ($ref 0 over 451 MB): color 126 distinct definitions, size 438, flavor 50.
Walmart.A value is stored as: inline on the member, typed by the slot's JSON Schema; governance is a description prefix: "Closed List - …" (enum) · "Alphanumeric, N characters - …" · "Number, Value range: A to B - …" · "Decimal, …".

Shopee.Built-in core (outside the bag): item fields: item_name REQ, description REQ, original_price REQ, weight REQ, item_sku, gtin_code, brand {brand_id int32 REQ, original_brand_name REQ}, dimension {package_height/length/width}, logistic_info REQ, seller_stock, price_info, tax / size chart / certification / purchase limit / complaint policy.
Shopee.Extension (the attribute): attribute_list, category-scoped: get_attribute_tree(category_id) → {attribute_id, name, mandatory, attribute_value_list[{value_id, name, value_unit, child_attribute_list}], attribute_info{input_type (5), input_validation_type (5), format_type (2), date_format_type, attribute_unit_list, max_value_count, is_oem, support_search_value}}; only last-level categories retrieve it.
Shopee.A value is stored as: value_id (shared row) or value_id: 0 + original_value_name (free text); a typed value carries value_unit.
Shopee.Brand: a reference to a platform-owned brand entity (brand_id).

Tokopedia.Built-in core (outside the bag): Era A: name ≤70, category_id, price, status, stock, min_order, weight, weight_unit, condition, sku ≤50, description ≤2000, dimension, etalase, variant. Era B: 34 depth-0 fields — title, description, category_id, brand_id, main_images, package_dimensions, package_weight, certifications, size_chart, …; price/inventory/identifier on the SKU.
Tokopedia.Extension (the attribute): Era A: the Annotation (“product specification based on category ID”) — group = a bare variant string, values[{id, name, data}]. Era B: GET /product/202309/categories/{id}/attributes → {id, name, type: SALES_PROPERTY|PRODUCT_PROPERTY, is_requried, values[{id, name, icon_url}], value_data_format, is_customizable, requirement_conditions[], is_multiple_selection}.
Tokopedia.A value is stored as: Era B: product_attributes[] {id, values[] {id, name}} — an id-bearing row or a name; all money/quantity fields string.
Tokopedia.Brand: Era A: none. Era B: platform-owned Brand entity (brand_id; “Brand does not exist” error).
Tokopedia.Cap: ambiguous — 12052525 “The attribute max num cannot exceed 3.”

Square.Built-in core (outside the bag): CatalogItem — 27 properties (name, description_html, categories, item_options, variations, product_type, is_alcoholic, kitchen_name, …); price / SKU / UPC on the variation (price_money, sku, upc, measurement_unit_id).
Square.Extension (the attribute): CatalogCustomAttributeDefinition — 12 properties; required type, name, allowed_object_types; key immutable; type ∈ STRING | BOOLEAN | NUMBER | SELECTION.
Square.Definition ↔ value: separate; value = CatalogObject.custom_attribute_values, a map keyed by the definition's key.
Square.A value is stored as: inline, typed by the definition: string_value / number_value / boolean_value / selection_uid_values — not a shared row.
Square.Brand: not answered ("cocoa_brand" only as a key example).
Square.Cap: 10 seller-visible + 10 seller-hidden definitions — live: the 11th → HTTP 400 ITEMS_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; scope (account vs app_id) unresolved.

Salesforce B2C.Extension (the attribute): three-level definition: ObjectTypeDefinition → ObjectAttributeGroup → ObjectAttributeDefinition with unit: String and valueTypeCode; system/custom switch = @system: xsd:boolean default="false"; REST prefixes custom attributes c_.
Salesforce B2C.Definition ↔ value: separate; which named facts are system vs custom is not answered.
Salesforce B2C.A value is stored as: typed by valueTypeCode (18: INT NUMBER STRING TEXT HTML DATE IMAGE BOOLEAN MONEY QUANTITY DATETIME EMAIL PASSWORD SET_OF_* ENUM_OF_*) vs the XSD's 16 (no MONEY/QUANTITY — the two disagree).
Salesforce B2C.Example:
◇ 
<custom-attributes><custom-attribute attribute-id="warrantyType">…</custom-attribute></custom-attributes>
— warrantyType in group ProductExtras is the only named pair in the record; no instance data retrieved (U9)

Akeneo.Built-in core (outside the bag): pim_catalog_product: uuid, id, identifier, enabled, raw_values, created, updated, rawQuantifiedAssociations + edges family, parent, familyVariant, groups, categories, associations. Everything describing content is an attribute — title (attributeAsLabel), price (pim_catalog_price_collection), images, SKU (pim_catalog_identifier), weight (pim_catalog_metric). Barcode: no such concept.
Akeneo.Extension (the attribute): pim_catalog_attribute, ~30 columns: type (19 CE types, immutable), is_required, is_unique, is_localizable, is_scopable, sortOrder, useableAsGridFilter, metricFamily, defaultMetricUnit, group; the Family decides the set (never the category).
Akeneo.Definition ↔ value: separate; option values are shared AttributeOption rows, but the product copies the code string — “referential integrity is a validator, not a foreign key”.
Akeneo.Brand: both — a pim_catalog_simpleselect attribute in the demo catalogue, and (EE) a Reference Entity with a label, logo, description, pages.
Akeneo.Example:
● 
"weight": [{"locale": null, "scope": null, "data": {"amount": "800.0000", "unit": "GRAM", "symbol": "g"}}]
(#11069 §2c); ◇ "color": [{"locale": null, "scope": null, "data": "red"}] — the option code copied as a string

WooCommerce.Built-in core (outside the bag): WordPress rows: post_title, post_excerpt; postmeta _sku, _global_unique_id (GTIN), _price. Shipping dimensions (_weight…) not answered (0 hits).
WooCommerce.Extension (the attribute): three objects: (1) per-product WC_Product_Attribute {id, name, options, position, visible, variation} serialised into one _product_attributes postmeta row; (2) global definition woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies {attribute_id, attribute_name, attribute_label, attribute_type, attribute_orderby, attribute_public}; (3) the value = a wp_terms row.
WooCommerce.Definition ↔ value: global attributes have a definition row; a product-local attribute has none (id 0; is_taxonomy() { return 0 < id }). No attribute-set object exists.
WooCommerce.A value is stored as: a term — “a bare label — six fields, none a quantity, a unit or a dimension” — shared across products; the variation copies the slug string.
WooCommerce.Brand: product_brand, a core taxonomy since 9.4.0 (2024-11-11) — the one merchant-owned brand entity in the thirteen.
WooCommerce.Example: ● attribute 3 = pa_flavour, variation:true on product 10 / false on product 22; variation 27 of product 11 stores attribute_pa_flavour = 'mint' (posted "option":"Mint" → 201, no term created) (#11080 §1.3, §2 step 6)

commercetools.Built-in core (outside the bag): ProductData 13: name, categories, categoryOrderHints?, description?, slug, metaTitle?, metaDescription?, metaKeywords?, masterVariant, variants, searchKeywords, attributes, defaultVariant?. ProductVariant 13: id, sku?, key?, prices?, attributes?, images?, assets?, availability?, … No barcode/GTIN field anywhere; weight is an ordinary attribute.
commercetools.Extension (the attribute): AttributeDefinition {type, name (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ 2..256), label, isRequired, attributeConstraint, inputTip?, inputHint, isSearchable, level} — not a resource (no id, no version), reached only through its ProductType.
commercetools.A value is stored as: value: any, typed by the definition's type (13 types); enum values {key, label} nested in the ProductType; {"name":"weight","value":250} — no unit.
commercetools.Cap: none per type; 50 Product + 50 Variant attributes indexable; 1,000 ProductTypes.
commercetools.Example:
● 
{"name": "weight", "value": 250}
(vendor sample, #11081 §2c — no unit); ◇ {"name": "color", "value": {"key": "red", "label": "Red"}} — the documented enum shape

Magento.Extension (the attribute): everything else is an eav_attribute row (17 columns: attribute_code, frontend_input, backend_type, source_model, is_user_defined, is_required, is_unique, default_value; UNIQUE (entity_type_id, attribute_code)) + overlay catalog_eav_attribute (24 columns); the default set installs 43 definitions.
Magento.Definition ↔ value: separate — and one registry, two storages: sku, created_at, updated_at have a definition row with backend_type = 'static' (isStatic()) while their value lives in a column.
Magento.A value is stored as: five typed tables — catalog_product_entity_{varchar,int,decimal,text,datetime}, UNIQUE (entity_id, attribute_id, store_id); select values = eav_attribute_option.option_id (int) with labels in eav_attribute_option_value per store view.
Magento.Brand: the installed manufacturer attribute (select, user_defined). Barcode: no vendor term.
Magento.Example:
● uid Y29uZmlndXJhYmxlLzkzLzUz = configurable/93/53: parent entity 93, option 53 on two surfaces of one response (#11082 §1.7); ◇ 
catalog_product_entity_int {entity_id: 93, attribute_id: 83, store_id: 0, value: 53}
eav_attribute_option_value {option_id: 53, store_id: 0, value: 'Red'} {option_id: 53, store_id: 2, value: 'Merah'}
